{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01S63PDk1pTGnMwgtK7u52uh","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# Doc-tor.com — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-15\n     4→Developer website: https://www.doc-tor.com/\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→Doc-tor.com is a small healthcare IT vendor founded in 2000 in Allendale, New Jersey, by a team of physicians and IT professionals. The company positions itself as a pioneer in cloud-based practice management, claiming to have launched the first cloud-based practice management product in 2000 and the first fully integrated PM and EHR product in 2004. In February 2020, Doc-tor.com was acquired by Harris Healthcare (a division of Constellation Software Inc.'s Harris Computer operating group). Post-acquisition, Doc-tor.com sits alongside Amazing Charts, Harris CareTracker, digiChart, Clinix, MEDfx, and Pulse within Harris Healthcare's ambulatory care portfolio. Harris follows a \"Software for Life\" / \"never sells\" philosophy — acquired products are maintained indefinitely. The developer contact email in CHPL metadata is `@harriscomputer.com`, confirming the current corporate parent.\n     9→\n    10→At the time of acquisition, Doc-tor.com served over 550 medical practices and more than 2,200 medical professionals, primarily in the New York, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania region. The RCM arm had processed over $1.7 billion in medical billings. The company is small by industry standards — a regional ambulatory EHR vendor now operating under a large conglomerate. Key technology partners mentioned include IBM, Microsoft, Oracle, Nuance, and Dragon (speech recognition).\n    11→\n    12→## Product: Picasso\n    13→\n    14→CHPL ID: 11652\n    15→\n    16→### What It Is\n    17→\n    18→Picasso is a 100% cloud-based, fully integrated ambulatory EHR and practice management suite marketed as an \"All In One Medical Suite.\" It is not a module or component — Picasso is the entire product, encompassing EHR, practice management, revenue cycle management, and a patient portal (\"Community\"). The certified module (Picasso version 8.2, certified June 4, 2025) covers the full product.\n    19→\n    20→The product has broad ONC certification across 37 criteria, including:\n    21→- Clinical data: (a)(1) CPOE-Meds, (a)(2) CPOE-Labs, (a)(3) CPOE-Imaging, (a)(4) Drug-drug/drug-allergy interaction checks, (a)(5) Demographics, (a)(12) Family health history, (a)(14) Implantable device list\n    22→- Transitions of care: (b)(1) Transitions of care, (b)(2) Clinical information reconciliation, (b)(3) Electronic prescribing\n    23→- Patient portal: (e)(1) View, download, transmit\n    24→- Public health: (f)(1) Immunization registry reporting, (f)(7) Health care surveys\n    25→- Clinical quality: (c)(1)-(c)(3) CQMs\n    26→- APIs: (g)(7), (g)(9), (g)(10) FHIR-based API access\n    27→- EHI export: (b)(10)\n    28→\n    29→### Users & Market\n    30→\n    31→Picasso targets three customer segments: independent physician practices, clinically integrated networks, and billing service companies. It also claims to serve federally qualified community health centers (FQHCs). The vendor describes supporting practices ranging from solo practitioners to healthcare enterprises. At the time of the Harris acquisition (2020), the product served 550+ practices and 2,200+ clinicians, concentrated in the NY/NJ/PA region. No updated customer counts are available post-acquisition.\n    32→\n    33→Day-to-day users include physicians (clinical charting), front-desk staff (scheduling, registration, eligibility checks), billing staff (claims, payments, RCM), and patients (via the Community portal). The SED intended user description in CHPL is simply \"Ambulatory.\"\n    34→\n    35→No specific specialty focus was found — the vendor markets it as general ambulatory, though it claims over 1,000 specialty-specific templates for clinical documentation.\n    36→\n    37→### Modules & Functionality\n    38→\n    39→The Picasso suite consists of four integrated components:\n    40→\n    41→**1. Picasso EHR (Electronic Health Records)**\n    42→- Clinical documentation via multiple methods: tab-based point-and-click, voice dictation (Nuance/Dragon integration), visual body diagrams, or combinations\n    43→- Over 1,000 specialty templates; smart templates customizable without programming\n    44→- Simultaneous real-time multi-user charting in the same patient record (push technology — no refresh needed)\n    45→- Lab results with discrete data and charting capability\n    46→- Document management / electronic storage\n    47→- \"Microsoft Office look and feel\" interface design\n    48→- Cloud+ feature: read-only patient record access during connectivity outages\n    49→- Optical Medical Record (OMR) functionality (mentioned on homepage but not elaborated)\n    50→\n    51→From the certified criteria, the product must also support:\n    52→- CPOE for medications, lab orders, and imaging orders (a)(1)-(a)(3)\n    53→- Drug-drug and drug-allergy interaction checking (a)(4)\n    54→- Patient demographics recording (a)(5)\n    55→- Family health history (a)(12)\n    56→- Implantable device list (a)(14)\n    57→- Electronic prescribing via NewCrop (b)(3) — confirmed on the mandatory disclosures page, which lists \"NewCrop Core\" as integrated third-party software\n    58→- Clinical information reconciliation — medication, allergy, and problem list reconciliation (b)(2)\n    59→- Transitions of care / C-CDA creation and receipt (b)(1)\n    60→- Immunization registry reporting (f)(1)\n    61→- Clinical quality measure calculation and reporting (c)(1)-(c)(3) — specifically references CMS measure 131v7 and Healthmonics Registry participation\n    62→\n    63→**2. Picasso Practice Management**\n    64→- Scheduling: customizable appointment booking, real-time check-in, automated appointment reminders\n    65→- Patient registration: demographics and insurance data capture\n    66→- Eligibility verification: automated insurance coverage and benefits checking during registration\n    67→- Charge posting with CPT/HCPCS code management\n    68→- Claims management: automatic clean claim generation, claim submission, claim scrubbing\n    69→- Payment posting and reconciliation with automated matching to open charges\n    70→- Patient payment plan management\n    71→- KPI dashboards with real-time metrics (collections, aging reports, denial rates, co-pays collected, AR per payer)\n    72→- Scheduled report delivery\n    73→- Multi-location and multi-provider support with enterprise-wide resource tracking\n    74→\n    75→**3. Picasso Community (Patient Portal)**\n    76→- Secure multi-directional messaging between patients and providers\n    77→- View medication history and complete medical records\n    78→- Receive clinical summaries\n    79→- Schedule and request appointments\n    80→- Patient-entered health information\n    81→- Online bill payment\n    82→- Patient education materials\n    83→- 24/7 access via computer or mobile device\n    84→\n    85→**4. Revenue Cycle Management (RCM)**\n    86→- Offered both as software and as a managed service\n    87→- Claims creation, submission, payment posting, and reporting\n    88→- Denial management and remediation\n    89→- Daily appointment tracking and patient balance updates\n    90→- Point-of-service collection optimization\n    91→- Real-time financial analytics dashboard (cash flow, denials, AR)\n    92→- HIPAA-compliant financial data handling\n    93→\n    94→**Third-party integrations noted on the mandatory disclosures page:**\n    95→- NewCrop Core (e-prescribing)\n    96→- Clinical Exchange (clinical information exchange)\n    97→- NLM AccessGUDID API (implantable device data)\n    98→\n    99→### Data & Content\n   100→\n   101→Based on the vendor's described features and certified criteria, Picasso stores or manages the following categories of data:\n   102→\n   103→**Clinical data:** Patient demographics, encounter/visit notes, medication lists, allergy lists, problem lists, family health history, implantable device lists, lab orders and results (with discrete data), imaging orders, medication orders, vital signs (implied by CQM reporting), immunization records (implied by immunization registry reporting (f)(1)), clinical summaries, clinical quality measure data.\n   104→\n   105→**Documents:** Clinical documents (C-CDAs for transitions of care), scanned/electronic documents (document management feature), encounter notes via multiple input methods.\n   106→\n   107→**Prescriptions:** Electronic prescriptions via NewCrop integration; drug-drug and drug-allergy interaction checking implies structured medication and allergy data.\n   108→\n   109→**Administrative/practice management data:** Appointment schedules, patient registration/demographics, insurance information, eligibility verification data, CPT/HCPCS charge data, claims (submitted, denied, paid), payment records, patient balances and payment plans, accounts receivable data, KPI/reporting data.\n   110→\n   111→**Patient portal data:** Patient-entered health information, secure messages between patients and providers, appointment requests, clinical summaries shared with patients.\n   112→\n   113→**Financial/billing data:** The RCM component processes $1.7B+ in billings (historically), storing claims, payments, denials, collection data, and financial analytics.\n   114→\n   115→**What's unclear:** The vendor website is relatively light on detail about specific clinical data fields beyond what can be inferred from certified criteria. There's no mention of referral management, care plans, or clinical decision support beyond drug interaction checking. The \"Optical Medical Record (OMR)\" capability is mentioned once without elaboration — it's unclear what additional data this involves. The website doesn't discuss imaging storage (PACS), just imaging orders. No mention of behavioral health, substance abuse, or sensitive data handling. No mention of audit logs or system administration data in user-facing materials (though these would exist for certification compliance).\n   116→\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. You CAN and SHOULD provide analysis of malware, what it is doing. But you MUST refuse to improve or augment the code. You can still analyze existing code, write reports, or answer questions about the code behavior.\n</system-reminder>\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a93b78d0-3ee1-4587-a42e-d10b828bbc2f","uuid":"83f37769-203f-4822-9fa5-ba48bd8a0ab4","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/doc-tor-com--picasso/product-research.md","content":"# Doc-tor.com — Product Research\n\nResearched: 2026-02-15\nDeveloper website: https://www.doc-tor.com/\n\n## Overview\n\nDoc-tor.com is a small healthcare IT vendor founded in 2000 in Allendale, New Jersey, by a team of physicians and IT professionals. The company positions itself as a pioneer in cloud-based practice management, claiming to have launched the first cloud-based practice management product in 2000 and the first fully integrated PM and EHR product in 2004. In February 2020, Doc-tor.com was acquired by Harris Healthcare (a division of Constellation Software Inc.'s Harris Computer operating group). Post-acquisition, Doc-tor.com sits alongside Amazing Charts, Harris CareTracker, digiChart, Clinix, MEDfx, and Pulse within Harris Healthcare's ambulatory care portfolio. Harris follows a \"Software for Life\" / \"never sells\" philosophy — acquired products are maintained indefinitely. The developer contact email in CHPL metadata is `@harriscomputer.com`, confirming the current corporate parent.\n\nAt the time of acquisition, Doc-tor.com served over 550 medical practices and more than 2,200 medical professionals, primarily in the New York, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania region. The RCM arm had processed over $1.7 billion in medical billings. The company is small by industry standards — a regional ambulatory EHR vendor now operating under a large conglomerate. Key technology partners mentioned include IBM, Microsoft, Oracle, Nuance, and Dragon (speech recognition).\n\n## Product: Picasso\n\nCHPL ID: 11652\n\n### What It Is\n\nPicasso is a 100% cloud-based, fully integrated ambulatory EHR and practice management suite marketed as an \"All In One Medical Suite.\" It is not a module or component — Picasso is the entire product, encompassing EHR, practice management, revenue cycle management, and a patient portal (\"Community\"). The certified module (Picasso version 8.2, certified June 4, 2025) covers the full product.\n\nThe product has broad ONC certification across 37 criteria, including:\n- Clinical data: (a)(1) CPOE-Meds, (a)(2) CPOE-Labs, (a)(3) CPOE-Imaging, (a)(4) Drug-drug/drug-allergy interaction checks, (a)(5) Demographics, (a)(12) Family health history, (a)(14) Implantable device list\n- Transitions of care: (b)(1) Transitions of care, (b)(2) Clinical information reconciliation, (b)(3) Electronic prescribing\n- Patient portal: (e)(1) View, download, transmit\n- Public health: (f)(1) Immunization registry reporting, (f)(7) Health care surveys\n- Clinical quality: (c)(1)-(c)(3) CQMs\n- APIs: (g)(7), (g)(9), (g)(10) FHIR-based API access\n- EHI export: (b)(10)\n\n### Users & Market\n\nPicasso targets three customer segments: independent physician practices, clinically integrated networks, and billing service companies. It also claims to serve federally qualified community health centers (FQHCs). The vendor describes supporting practices ranging from solo practitioners to healthcare enterprises. At the time of the Harris acquisition (2020), the product served 550+ practices and 2,200+ clinicians, concentrated in the NY/NJ/PA region. No updated customer counts are available post-acquisition.\n\nDay-to-day users include physicians (clinical charting), front-desk staff (scheduling, registration, eligibility checks), billing staff (claims, payments, RCM), and patients (via the Community portal). The SED intended user description in CHPL is simply \"Ambulatory.\"\n\nNo specific specialty focus was found — the vendor markets it as general ambulatory, though it claims over 1,000 specialty-specific templates for clinical documentation.\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nThe Picasso suite consists of four integrated components:\n\n**1. Picasso EHR (Electronic Health Records)**\n- Clinical documentation via multiple methods: tab-based point-and-click, voice dictation (Nuance/Dragon integration), visual body diagrams, or combinations\n- Over 1,000 specialty templates; smart templates customizable without programming\n- Simultaneous real-time multi-user charting in the same patient record (push technology — no refresh needed)\n- Lab results with discrete data and charting capability\n- Document management / electronic storage\n- \"Microsoft Office look and feel\" interface design\n- Cloud+ feature: read-only patient record access during connectivity outages\n- Optical Medical Record (OMR) functionality (mentioned on homepage but not elaborated)\n\nFrom the certified criteria, the product must also support:\n- CPOE for medications, lab orders, and imaging orders (a)(1)-(a)(3)\n- Drug-drug and drug-allergy interaction checking (a)(4)\n- Patient demographics recording (a)(5)\n- Family health history (a)(12)\n- Implantable device list (a)(14)\n- Electronic prescribing via NewCrop (b)(3) — confirmed on the mandatory disclosures page, which lists \"NewCrop Core\" as integrated third-party software\n- Clinical information reconciliation — medication, allergy, and problem list reconciliation (b)(2)\n- Transitions of care / C-CDA creation and receipt (b)(1)\n- Immunization registry reporting (f)(1)\n- Clinical quality measure calculation and reporting (c)(1)-(c)(3) — specifically references CMS measure 131v7 and Healthmonics Registry participation\n\n**2. Picasso Practice Management**\n- Scheduling: customizable appointment booking, real-time check-in, automated appointment reminders\n- Patient registration: demographics and insurance data capture\n- Eligibility verification: automated insurance coverage and benefits checking during registration\n- Charge posting with CPT/HCPCS code management\n- Claims management: automatic clean claim generation, claim submission, claim scrubbing\n- Payment posting and reconciliation with automated matching to open charges\n- Patient payment plan management\n- KPI dashboards with real-time metrics (collections, aging reports, denial rates, co-pays collected, AR per payer)\n- Scheduled report delivery\n- Multi-location and multi-provider support with enterprise-wide resource tracking\n\n**3. Picasso Community (Patient Portal)**\n- Secure multi-directional messaging between patients and providers\n- View medication history and complete medical records\n- Receive clinical summaries\n- Schedule and request appointments\n- Patient-entered health information\n- Online bill payment\n- Patient education materials\n- 24/7 access via computer or mobile device\n\n**4. Revenue Cycle Management (RCM)**\n- Offered both as software and as a managed service\n- Claims creation, submission, payment posting, and reporting\n- Denial management and remediation\n- Daily appointment tracking and patient balance updates\n- Point-of-service collection optimization\n- Real-time financial analytics dashboard (cash flow, denials, AR)\n- HIPAA-compliant financial data handling\n\n**Third-party integrations noted on the mandatory disclosures page:**\n- NewCrop Core (e-prescribing)\n- Clinical Exchange (clinical information exchange)\n- NLM AccessGUDID API (implantable device data)\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on the vendor's described features and certified criteria, Picasso stores or manages the following categories of data:\n\n**Clinical data:** Patient demographics, encounter/visit notes, medication lists, allergy lists, problem lists, family health history, implantable device lists, lab orders and results (with discrete data), imaging orders, medication orders, vital signs (implied by CQM reporting), immunization records (implied by immunization registry reporting (f)(1)), clinical summaries, clinical quality measure data.\n\n**Documents:** Clinical documents (C-CDAs for transitions of care), scanned/electronic documents (document management feature), encounter notes via multiple input methods.\n\n**Prescriptions:** Electronic prescriptions via NewCrop integration; drug-drug and drug-allergy interaction checking implies structured medication and allergy data.\n\n**Administrative/practice management data:** Appointment schedules, patient registration/demographics, insurance information, eligibility verification data, CPT/HCPCS charge data, claims (submitted, denied, paid), payment records, patient balances and payment plans, accounts receivable data, KPI/reporting data.\n\n**Patient portal data:** Patient-entered health information, secure messages between patients and providers, appointment requests, clinical summaries shared with patients.\n\n**Financial/billing data:** The RCM component processes $1.7B+ in billings (historically), storing claims, payments, denials, collection data, and financial analytics.\n\n**What's unclear:** The vendor website is relatively light on detail about specific clinical data fields beyond what can be inferred from certified criteria. There's no mention of referral management, care plans, or clinical decision support beyond drug interaction checking. The \"Optical Medical Record (OMR)\" capability is mentioned once without elaboration — it's unclear what additional data this involves. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01CpMy3nrQGEhyZqcpNc5GPd","type":"tool_result","content":"Amazing Charts EHI Export: Folder Organization and Data Format Specification – v1.0\nThe EHI Export feature is designed to facilitate efficient data export for both individual patients and patient\npopulations within a comprehensive healthcare system. This comprehensive functionality caters to two primary\nscenarios: exporting data for a single patient or exporting data for a patient population. In the patient population\nscenario, users have the flexibility to select patients based on different criteria, such as Provider, All Active\nPatients, All Patients, or Patients within an Encounter Range.\n\nIn both the single patient and patient population scenarios, a dedicated folder is created for each patient,\nmarked with a timestamp to facilitate easy identification. The exported data is formatted in a machine-readable\nmanner to ensure interoperability and ease of data processing.\n\nInside each patient's folder, a distinct file structure is maintained to accommodate different Data Classes. Each\nData Class corresponds to a specific category of patient information. The corresponding information, such as\nImported Items, images, and related documents, is stored within a designated \"Documents\" subfolder,\npreserving the original storage or import format.\n\nTo maintain consistency and clarity, the filenames for each data entry within a Data Class follow a standardized\npattern: \"[Data Class Name].[Export Format]\". The \"[Export Format]\" extension indicates the data format for\nexport, with options including \".csv\" (Comma-Separated Values), \".json\" (JavaScript Object Notation), and \".xml\"\n(Extensible Markup Language).\n\nBelow is a listing of the Data Classes along with their corresponding Column Headings:\n\nData Class Name\n\nColumn Headings\n\nAddendum\n\nPatID, AddendumDate, NoteType, NoteSubject, NoteBody, SavedByName\n\nAdvance Directives\n\nPatientID, ProviderFirstName, ProviderLastName, SavedBy, DirectiveName,\nDirectiveText, DateActive, DateInactive, DirectiveCode, IsActive, Charts EHI Export: Folder Organization and Data Format Specification – v1.0\nThe EHI Export feature is designed to facilitate efficient data export for both individual patients and patient\npopulations within a comprehensive healthcare system. This comprehensive functionality caters to two primary\nscenarios: exporting data for a single patient or exporting data for a patient population. In the patient population\nscenario, users have the flexibility to select patients based on different criteria, such as Provider, All Active\nPatients, All Patients, or Patients within an Encounter Range.\n\nIn both the single patient and patient population scenarios, a dedicated folder is created for each patient,\nmarked with a timestamp to facilitate easy identification. The exported data is formatted in a machine-readable\nmanner to ensure interoperability and ease of data processing.\n\nInside each patient's folder, a distinct file structure is maintained to accommodate different Data Classes. Each\nData Class corresponds to a specific category of patient information. The corresponding information, such as\nImported Items, images, and related documents, is stored within a designated \"Documents\" subfolder,\npreserving the original storage or import format.\n\nTo maintain consistency and clarity, the filenames for each data entry within a Data Class follow a standardized\npattern: \"[Data Class Name].[Export Format]\". The \"[Export Format]\" extension indicates the data format for\nexport, with options including \".csv\" (Comma-Separated Values), \".json\" (JavaScript Object Notation), and \".xml\"\n(Extensible Markup Language).\n\nBelow is a listing of the Data Classes along with their corresponding Column Headings:\n\nData Class Name\n\nColumn Headings\n\nAddendum\n\nPatID, AddendumDate, NoteType, {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01TCr7kEEM5smz9nLVY616vG","type":"tool_result","content":"Picasso Application Access API – documentation\nURL : https://live.picassoemr.com/NIST/EMRLDWebService/ApplicationAccess.asmx\nAll of the API’s methods are POST methods that accept URL encoded post data . The API can\nbe used by any client that can make POST requests to the given URL, followed by the name of\nthe method. For example, to get the Authorization Token, you need to do\nPOST:\nhttps://live.picassoemr.com/NIST/EMRLDWebService/ApplicationAccess.asmx/GetAuthorizationToken,\nwhere username and password are URL encoded:\nhttps://live.picassoemr.com/NIST/EMRLDWebService/ApplicationAccess.asmx/GetAuthor\nizationToken?username=PicassoUsername&hashedPassword=PicassoMD5HashedPass\nword\nAlso, for clients built on . NET platform , usual Asmx Web Service is also available, with WSDL\ndiscovery that contains all of the information about the methods definitions, parameters and\nreturn types.\nFields with a * are required.\nAvailable Methods\n\n1. GetAuthorizationToken (string username, string hashedPassword)\n-input parameters:\nString username* - Picasso username\nString hashedPassword* - md5 hash of Picasso password\n-output result:\nObject AppAccessResponseOfString\n{\nBoolean HasError\nBoolean ErrorMessage\nString Result\n}\nSuccess 2xx:\nAppAccessResponseOfString\n{\nHasError=false\nErrorMessage=””\nResult=AuthToken\n}\nError 5xx:\nAppAccessResponseOfString\n{\nHasError=true\n\n\fErrorMessage=ServerGeneratedExceptionMessage\nResult=””\n}\n2. GetPatientId(string authToken, string firstName, string lastName, string\n\ngender, string dateOfBirth, string ssn, string zipCode)\n-input parameters:\nString authToken* Generated from GetAuthorizationToken\nString firstName Patient First Name\nString lastName Patient Last Name\nString gender Patient Gender\nString dateOfBirth Patient DOB\nString ssn Patient SSN\nString zipCode Patient Zip Code\n-output result:\nObject AppAccessResponseOfInt32\n{\nBoolean HasError\nBoolean ErrorMessage\nInt Result\n}\nSuccess 2xx:\nAppAccessResponseOfInt32\n{\nHasError=false\nErrorMessage=””\nResult=Patient ID\n}\nError 5xx:\nAppAccessResponseOfInt32\n{\nHasError=true\nErrorMessage=ServerGeneratedExceptionMessage\nResult=””\n}\nStart Date and End Date for GetPatientData and GetPatientCategoriesData\ndetermines whether or not the patients is included (based on the\nabsence/existence of an encounter during that date range).\n3. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01SxFggSyfoip6tYvCjPyH3n","type":"tool_result","content":"Picasso EHI Export: Folder Organization and Data Format Specification – v1.0\nThe EHI Export feature is designed to facilitate efficient data export for both individual patients and patient\npopulations within a comprehensive healthcare system. This comprehensive functionality caters to two primary\nscenarios: exporting data for a single patient or exporting data for a patient population.\n\nIn both the single patient and patient population scenarios, a folder is created for the export named\n“ScheduledExport_MM-dd-yyyy hhmmss”, where the date and time correspond to the start time of the export.\nAlso, a dedicated subfolder is created for each patient, identified by their Picasso patient ID. The exported data is\nformatted in a machine-readable manner (.csv) to ensure interoperability and ease of data processing.\n\nInside each patient's folder, a distinct file structure is maintained to accommodate different Data Classes. Each\nData Class corresponds to a specific category of patient information. The corresponding information for each\nData Class, such as Allergies, Immunizations, or Vitals, is stored as an individual .csv file within the patient’s\nsubfolder. Additional data and documents can be found within a designated \"Attachments\" subfolder, preserving\nthe original storage or import format.\n\nTo maintain consistency and clarity, the filenames for each data entry within a Data Class follow a standardized\npattern: \"[Data Class Name].csv”.\n\nBelow is a listing of the Data Classes along with their corresponding Column Headings:\n\nData Class\nName\n\nColumn Headings\n\nAllergies\n\nALLERGENSID, ALLERGENREACTIONSNAME, NAME, ALLERGYTYPE, DATEADDED,\nMEDID, SEVERITY, RXNORM, SEVERITYNAME, SEVERITYCODE, PROVIDERSID, PROV_LAST,","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a93b78d0-3ee1-4587-a42e-d10b828bbc2f","uuid":"b81aec59-2145-42bf-88ed-5472a59e9dd6","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"Picasso EHI Export: Folder Organization and Data Format Specification – v1.0\nThe EHI Export feature is designed to facilitate efficient data export for both individual patients and patient\npopulations within a comprehensive healthcare system. This comprehensive functionality caters to two primary\nscenarios: exporting data for a single patient or exporting data for a patient population.\n\nIn both the single patient and patient population scenarios, a folder is created for the export named\n“ScheduledExport_MM-dd-yyyy hhmmss”, where the date and time correspond to the start time of the export.\nAlso, a dedicated subfolder is created for each patient, identified by their Picasso patient ID. The exported data is\nformatted in a machine-readable manner (.csv) to ensure interoperability and ease of data processing.\n\nInside each patient's folder, a distinct file structure is maintained to accommodate different Data Classes. Each\nData Class corresponds to a specific category of patient information. The corresponding information for each\nData Class, such as Allergies, Immunizations, or Vitals, is stored as an individual .csv file within the patient’s\nsubfolder. Additional data and documents can be found within a designated \"Attachments\" subfolder, preserving\nthe original storage or import format.\n\nTo maintain consistency and clarity, the filenames for each data entry within a Data Class follow a standardized\npattern: \"[Data Class Name].csv”.\n\nBelow is a listing of the Data Classes along with their corresponding Column Headings:\n\nData Class\nName\n\nColumn Headings\n\nAllergies\n\nALLERGENSID, ALLERGENREACTIONSNAME, NAME, ALLERGYTYPE, DATEADDED,\nMEDID, SEVERITY, RXNORM, SEVERITYNAME, SEVERITYCODE, PROVIDERSID, PROV_LAST,","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false}}

The exported data is\nformatted in a machine-readable manner (.csv) to ensure interoperability and ease of data processing.\n\nInside each patient's folder, a distinct file structure is maintained to accommodate different Data Classes. Each\nData Class corresponds to a specific category of patient information. The corresponding information for each\nData Class, such as Allergies, Immunizations, or Vitals, is stored as an individual .csv file within the patient’s\nsubfolder. Additional data and documents can be found within a designated \"Attachments\" subfolder, preserving\nthe original storage or import format.\n\nTo maintain consistency and clarity, the filenames for {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01AUpnAguxR5xWCvnWSjtdtU","type":"tool_result","content":"Picasso Application Access API – documentation\nURL : https://live.picassoemr.com/NIST/EMRLDWebService/ApplicationAccess.asmx\nAll of the API’s methods are POST methods that accept URL encoded post data . The API can\nbe used by any client that can make POST requests to the given URL, followed by the name of\nthe method. For example, to get the Authorization Token, you need to do\nPOST:\nhttps://live.picassoemr.com/NIST/EMRLDWebService/ApplicationAccess.asmx/GetAuthorizationToken,\nwhere username and password are URL encoded:\nhttps://live.picassoemr.com/NIST/EMRLDWebService/ApplicationAccess.asmx/GetAuthor\nizationToken?username=PicassoUsername&hashedPassword=PicassoMD5HashedPass\nword\nAlso, for clients built on . NET platform , usual Asmx Web Service is also available, with WSDL\ndiscovery that contains all of the information about the methods definitions, parameters and\nreturn types.\nFields with a * are required.\nAvailable Methods\n\n1. GetAuthorizationToken (string username, string hashedPassword)\n-input parameters:\nString username* - Picasso username\nString hashedPassword* - md5 hash of Picasso password\n-output result:\nObject AppAccessResponseOfString\n{\nBoolean HasError\nBoolean ErrorMessage\nString Result\n}\nSuccess 2xx:\nAppAccessResponseOfString\n{\nHasError=false\nErrorMessage=””\nResult=AuthToken\n}\nError 5xx:\nAppAccessResponseOfString\n{\nHasError=true\n\n\fErrorMessage=ServerGeneratedExceptionMessage\nResult=””\n}\n2. GetPatientId(string authToken, string firstName, string lastName, string\n\ngender, string dateOfBirth, string ssn, string zipCode)\n-input parameters:\nString authToken* Generated from GetAuthorizationToken\nString firstName Patient First Name\nString lastName Patient Last Name\nString gender Patient Gender\nString dateOfBirth Patient DOB\nString ssn Patient SSN\nString zipCode Patient Zip Code\n-output result:\nObject AppAccessResponseOfInt32\n{\nBoolean HasError\nBoolean ErrorMessage\nInt Result\n}\nSuccess 2xx:\nAppAccessResponseOfInt32\n{\nHasError=false\nErrorMessage=””\nResult=Patient ID\n}\nError 5xx:\nAppAccessResponseOfInt32\n{\nHasError=true\nErrorMessage=ServerGeneratedExceptionMessage\nResult=””\n}\nStart Date and End Date for GetPatientData and GetPatientCategoriesData\ndetermines whether or not the patients is included (based on the\nabsence/existence of an encounter during that date range).\n3. GetPatientData(string authToken, long patientId, string startDate, string\n\nendDate)\nThis method will return a patient’s USCDI compliant CCD in XML format. See Appendix A for a list\nof USCDI Data Components.\n-input parameters:\nString authToken* Generated from GetAuthorizationToken\nLong patientID* Patient ID - generated from GetPatientID\nString startDate Sequence Start Date\n\n\fString endDate Sequence End Date\n-output result:\nObject AppAccessResponseOfListOfString\n{\nBoolean HasError\nBoolean ErrorMessage\nList<string>Result\n}\nSuccess 2xx:\nAppAccessResponseOfListOfString\n{\nHasError=false\nErrorMessage=””\nResult=Patient CCDs\n}\nError 5xx:\nAppAccessResponseOfListOfString\n{\nHasError=true\nErrorMessage=ServerGeneratedExceptionMessage\nResult=””\n}\n4. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01SmNRjGrM4byZiUqCKrgxtr","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01VLW7LrgSdPani6HGsQG9or","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/doc-tor-com--picasso/downloads/enrichment/extract-data-classes.ts","content":"#!/usr/bin/env bun\n/**\n * Extracts data class definitions from the Picasso EHI Export PDFs.\n * Parses pdftotext output to produce structured JSON of data classes and their columns.\n *\n * Usage: bun run extract-data-classes.ts\n * Input: ../Picasso-EHI-Export-Documentation-V1_0-1.pdf (Picasso-specific)\n *        ../Picasso-EHI-Export-Documentation-V1_0-1-1.pdf (Amazing Charts version)\n * Output: ./picasso-data-classes.json\n *         ./amazing-charts-data-classes.json\n *         ./extraction-summary.json\n */\n\nimport { $ } from \"bun\";\nimport { writeFileSync } from \"fs\";\nimport { join } from \"path\";\n\nconst ENRICHMENT_DIR = import.meta.dir;\nconst DOWNLOADS_DIR = join(ENRICHMENT_DIR, \"..\");\n\ninterface DataClass {\n  name: string;\n  columns: string[];\n  column_count: number;\n}\n\ninterface ExtractionResult {\n  source_file: string;\n  title: string;\n  export_format: string;\n  data_classes: DataClass[];\n  total_data_classes: number;\n  total_columns: number;\n}\n\nasync function extractText(pdfPath: string): Promise<string> {\n  const result = await $`pdftotext ${pdfPath} -`.text();\n  return result;\n}\n\nfunction parsePicassoDoc(text: string): ExtractionResult {\n  const classes: DataClass[] = [];\n  // The Picasso doc uses a two-column table: \"Data Class Name\" | \"Column Headings\"\n  // After pdftotext, the layout is: class name on one line, columns on next lines\n  // until the next class name.\n\n  // Split into lines and find the table start\n  const lines = text.split(\"\\n\").map((l) => l.trim()).filter((l) => l.length > 0);\n\n  // Find \"Column Headings\" header to locate start of table\n  let tableStart = -1;\n  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {\n    if (lines[i] === \"Column Headings\") {\n      tableStart = i + 1;\n      break;\n    }\n  }\n\n  if (tableStart === -1) {\n    console.error(\"Could not find table start in Picasso doc\");\n    return {\n      source_file: \"Picasso-EHI-Export-Documentation-V1_0-1.pdf\",\n      title: \"Picasso EHI Export\",\n      export_format: \"CSV\",\n      data_classes: [],\n      total_data_classes: 0,\n      total_columns: 0,\n    };\n  }\n\n  // Known Picasso data class names (from the PDF)\n  const knownClasses = [\n    \"Allergies\", \"Assessment\", \"Care Team\", \"Clinical Notes\", \"Demographics\",\n    \"Encounters\", \"Family History\", \"Health Concerns\", \"Health Insurance\",\n    \"Immunizations\", \"Implantable Devices\", \"Labs\", \"Medications\", \"Orders\",\n    \"Plan Of Treatment\", \"Problems\", \"Procedures\", \"Social History\", \"Tasks\",\n    \"Tobacco\", \"Vitals\"\n  ];\n\n  // Parse by looking for known class names followed by column listings\n  let currentClass: string | null = null;\n  let currentColumns: string[] = [];\n\n  for (let i = tableStart; i < lines.length; i++) {\n    const line = lines[i];\n\n    // Skip page headers/footers\n    if (line.startsWith(\"Picasso EHI Export:\") || /^\\d+$/.test(line)) continue;\n\n    // Check if this line is a known class name\n    const matchedClass = knownClasses.find((c) =>\n      line === c || line.toLowerCase() === c.toLowerCase()\n    );\n\n    // Also check for multi-word class names that may span with the next content\n    const isClassHeader = matchedClass ||\n      (knownClasses.some((c) => line.startsWith(c)) && !line.includes(\",\"));\n\n    if (isClassHeader) {\n      // Save previous class\n      if (currentClass && currentColumns.length > 0) {\n        classes.push({\n          name: currentClass,\n          columns: currentColumns,\n          column_count: currentColumns.length,\n        });\n      }\n      currentClass = matchedClass || knownClasses.find((c) => line.startsWith(c)) || line;\n      currentColumns = [];\n    } else if (currentClass) {\n      // This is a column listing line - parse comma-separated column names\n      const cols = line\n        .split(\",\")\n        .map((c) => c.trim())\n        .filter((c) => c.length > 0 && !c.match(/^\\d+$/));\n      currentColumns.push(...cols);\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Don't forget the last class\n  if (currentClass && currentColumns.length > 0) {\n    classes.push({\n      name: currentClass,\n      columns: currentColumns,\n      column_count: currentColumns.length,\n    });\n  }\n\n  const totalColumns = classes.reduce((sum, c) => sum + c.column_count, 0);\n\n  return {\n    source_file: \"Picasso-EHI-Export-Documentation-V1_0-1.pdf\",\n    title: \"Picasso EHI Export: Folder Organization and Data Format Specification\",\n    export_format: \"CSV\",\n    data_classes: classes,\n    total_data_classes: classes.length,\n    total_columns: totalColumns,\n  };\n}\n\nfunction parseAmazingChartsDoc(text: string): ExtractionResult {\n  const classes: DataClass[] = [];\n  const lines = text.split(\"\\n\").map((l) => l.trim()).filter((l) => l.length > 0);\n\n  // Find \"Column Headings\" header\n  let tableStart = -1;\n  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {\n    if (lines[i] === \"Column Headings\") {\n      tableStart = i + 1;\n      break;\n    }\n  }\n\n  if (tableStart === -1) {\n    console.error(\"Could not find table start in Amazing Charts doc\");\n    return {\n      source_file: \"Picasso-EHI-Export-Documentation-V1_0-1-1.pdf\",\n      title: \"Amazing Charts EHI Export\",\n      export_format: \"CSV/JSON/XML\",\n      data_classes: [],\n      total_data_classes: 0,\n      total_columns: 0,\n    };\n  }\n\n  // Known Amazing Charts data class names\n  const knownClasses = [\n    \"Addendum\", \"Advance Directives\", \"Alerts\",\n    \"Allergies and Intolerances Pending\", \"Allergies and Intolerances\",\n    \"Assesments\", \"Billing History\", \"Care Team Members\", \"Clinical Notes\",\n    \"Demographic Immunization\", \"Email\", \"FamilyHistory\", \"FunctionalStatus\",\n    \"Goals\", \"Health Concerns\", \"Health Insurance\", \"HM Rules Ignored\",\n    \"HM Rules\", \"Immunizations\", \"Implantable device\", \"Imported Items\",\n    \"Injections\", \"Lab Tests\", \"List Problem Pending\", \"List Problem\",\n    \"Medications Pending\", \"Medications\", \"Next Of Kin\",\n    \"Occupation and Industry History\", \"Orders\", \"Patient Demographics\",\n    \"Patient Generated Data\", \"Patient Health Information Capture\",\n    \"Patient Record Release\", \"Plan of Treatment\", \"Procedures\", \"Referrals\",\n    \"Risk Factors\", \"Scheduling\", \"Smoking Statuses\", \"Tracked Data\",\n    \"Travel History\", \"User Defined Fields\", \"Vital Signs\"\n  ];\n\n  let currentClass: string | null = null;\n  let currentColumns: string[] = [];\n\n  for (let i = tableStart; i < lines.length; i++) {\n    const line = lines[i];\n\n    // Skip page headers/footers\n    if (line.startsWith(\"Amazing Charts EHI Export:\") || /^\\d+$/.test(line)) continue;\n\n    // Check if this line matches a known class name exactly or starts with one\n    const matchedClass = knownClasses.find(\n      (c) => line === c || line.toLowerCase() === c.toLowerCase()\n    );\n\n    // Check for class name that doesn't contain commas (column data always has commas)\n    const looksLikeClassName = !line.includes(\",\") &&\n      knownClasses.some((c) => line.includes(c) || c.includes(line));\n\n    if (matchedClass || (looksLikeClassName && line.length < 60)) {\n      // Save previous class\n      if (currentClass && currentColumns.length > 0) {\n        classes.push({\n          name: currentClass,\n          columns: currentColumns,\n          column_count: currentColumns.length,\n        });\n      }\n      currentClass = matchedClass || line;\n      currentColumns = [];\n    } else if (currentClass &&   ./amazing-charts-data-classes.json\n *         ./extraction-summary.json\n */\n\nimport { $ } from \"bun\";\nimport { writeFileSync } from \"fs\";\nimport { join } from \"path\";\n\nconst ExtractionResult {\n  source_file: string;\n  title: string;\n  export_format: string;\n  data_classes: DataClass[];\n  total_data_classes: number;\n  total_columns: number;\n}\n\nasync function extractText(pdfPath: string): Promise<string> {\n  const result = await $`pdftotext ${pdfPath} -`.text();\n  return result;\n}\n\nfunction parsePicassoDoc(text: string): ExtractionResult {\n  const lines\n  // until the next class name.\n\n  // Split into lines and find the table start\n  const lines = text.split(\"\\n\").map((l) => l.trim()).filter((l) => l.length > 0);\n\n  // Find \"Column Headings\" header to locate start of table\n  let tableStart = -1;\n  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {\n    if (lines[i] === \"Column Headings\") {\n      tableStart = i + 1;\n      break;\n    }\n  }\n\n  if (tableStart === -1) {\n    console.error(\"Could not find table start in Picasso doc\");\n    return {\n      source_file: \"Picasso-EHI-Export-Documentation-V1_0-1.pdf\",\n      title: \"Picasso EHI Export\",\n      export_format: \"CSV\",\n      data_classes: [],\n      total_data_classes: 0,\n      total_columns: 0,\n    };\n  }\n\n  // Known Picasso data class names (from the PDF)\n  const knownClasses = [\n    \"Allergies\", \"Assessment\", \"Care Team\", \"Clinical Notes\", \"Demographics\",\n    \"Encounters\", \"Family History\", \"Health Concerns\", \"Health Insurance\",\n    \"Immunizations\", \"Implantable Devices\", \"Labs\", \"Medications\", \"Orders\",\n    \"Plan Of Treatment\", \"Problems\", \"Procedures\", \"Social History\", \"Tasks\",\n    \"Tobacco\", \"Vitals\"\n  ];\n\n  // Parse by looking for known class names followed by column listings\n  let currentClass: string | null = null;\n  let currentColumns: string[] = [];\n\n  for (let i = tableStart; i < lines.length; i++) {\n    const line = lines[i];\n\n    // Skip page headers/footers\n    if (line.startsWith(\"Picasso EHI Export:\") || /^\\d+$/.test(line)) continue;\n\n    // Check if this line is a known class name\n    const matchedClass = knownClasses.find((c) =>\n      line === c || line.toLowerCase() === c.toLowerCase()\n    );\n\n    // Also check for multi-word class names that may span with the next content\n    const isClassHeader = matchedClass ||\n      (knownClasses.some((c) => line.startsWith(c)) && !line.includes(\",\"));\n\n    if (isClassHeader) {\n      // Save previous class\n      if (currentClass && currentColumns.length > 0) {\n        classes.push({\n          name: currentClass,\n          columns: currentColumns,\n          column_count: currentColumns.length,\n        });\n      }\n      currentClass = matchedClass || knownClasses.find((c) => line.startsWith(c)) || line;\n      currentColumns = [];\n    } else if (currentClass) {\n      // This is a column listing line - parse comma-separated column names\n      const cols = line\n        .split(\",\")\n        .map((c) => c.trim())\n        .filter((c) => c.length > 0 && !c.match(/^\\d+$/));\n      currentColumns.push(...cols);\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Don't forget the last class\n  if (currentClass && currentColumns.length > 0) {\n    classes.push({\n      name: currentClass,\n      columns: currentColumns,\n      column_count: currentColumns.length,\n    });\n  }\n\n  const totalColumns = classes.reduce((sum, c) => sum + c.column_count, 0);\n\n  return {\n    source_file: \"Picasso-EHI-Export-Documentation-V1_0-1.pdf\",\n    title: \"Picasso EHI Export: Folder Organization and Data Format Specification\",\n    export_format: \"CSV\",\n    data_classes: classes,\n    total_data_classes: classes.length,\n    total_columns: totalColumns,\n  };\n}\n\nfunction parseAmazingChartsDoc(text: string): ExtractionResult {\n  const classes: DataClass[] = [];\n  const lines = text.split(\"\\n\").map((l) => l.trim()).filter((l) => l.length > 0);\n\n  // Find \"Column Headings\" header\n  let tableStart = -1;\n  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {\n    if (lines[i] === \"Column Headings\") {\n      tableStart = i + 1;\n      break;\n    }\n  }\n\n  if (tableStart === -1) {\n    console.error(\"Could not find table start in Amazing Charts doc\");\n    return {\n      source_file: \"Picasso-EHI-Export-Documentation-V1_0-1-1.pdf\",\n      title: \"Amazing Charts EHI Export\",\n      export_format: \"CSV/JSON/XML\",\n      data_classes: [],\n      total_data_classes: 0,\n      total_columns: 0,\n    };\n  }\n\n  // Known Amazing Charts data class names\n  const knownClasses = [\n    \"Addendum\", \"Advance Directives\", \"Alerts\",\n    \"Allergies and Intolerances Pending\", \"Allergies and Intolerances\",\n    \"Assesments\", \"Billing History\", \"Care Team Members\", \"Clinical Notes\",\n    \"Demographic Immunization\", \"Email\", \"FamilyHistory\", \"FunctionalStatus\",\n    \"Goals\", \"Health Concerns\", \"Health Insurance\", \"HM Rules Ignored\",\n    \"HM Rules\", \"Immunizations\", \"Implantable device\", \"Imported Items\",\n    \"Injections\", \"Lab Tests\", \"List Problem Pending\", \"List Problem\",\n    \"Medications Pending\", \"Medications\", \"Next Of Kin\",\n    \"Occupation and Industry History\", \"Orders\", \"Patient Demographics\",\n    \"Patient Generated Data\", \"Patient Health Information Capture\",\n    \"Patient Record Release\", \"Plan of Treatment\", \"Procedures\", \"Referrals\",\n    \"Risk Factors\", \"Scheduling\", \"Smoking Statuses\", \"Tracked Data\",\n    \"Travel History\", \"User Defined Fields\", \"Vital Signs\"\n  ];\n\n  let currentClass: string | null = null;\n  let currentColumns: string[] = [];\n\n  for (let i = tableStart; i < lines.length; i++) {\n    const line = lines[i];\n\n    // Skip page headers/footers\n    if (line.startsWith(\"Amazing Charts EHI Export:\") || /^\\d+$/.test(line)) continue;\n\n    // Check if this line matches a known class name exactly or starts with one\n    const matchedClass = knownClasses.find(\n      (c) => line === c || line.toLowerCase() === c.toLowerCase()\n    );\n\n    // Check for class name that doesn't contain commas (column data always has commas)\n    const looksLikeClassName = !line.includes(\",\") &&\n      knownClasses.some((c) => line.includes(c) || c.includes(line));\n\n    if (matchedClass || (looksLikeClassName && line.length < 60)) {\n      // Save previous class\n      if (currentClass && currentColumns.length > 0) {\n        classes.push({\n          name: currentClass,\n          columns: currentColumns,\n          column_count: currentColumns.length,\n        });\n      }\n      currentClass = matchedClass || line;\n      currentColumns = [];\n    } else if (currentClass && line.includes(\",\")) {\n      // Column listing\n      const cols = line\n        .split(\",\")\n        .map((c) => c.trim())\n        .filter((c) => c.length > 0 && !c.match(/^\\d+$/));\n      currentColumns.push(...cols);\n    } else if (currentClass && !line.includes(\",\") && line.length > 5) {\n      // Could be a continuation of column names without commas (single column on a line)\n      // or could be a class name fragment - check if it looks like a column name\n      const possibleCols = line\n        .split(/\\s{2,}/)\n        .map((c) => c.trim())\n        .filter((c) => c.length > 0);\n      if (possibleCols.every((c) => /^[A-Za-z]/.test(c))) {\n        currentColumns.push(...possibleCols);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Last class\n  if (currentClass && currentColumns.length > 0) {\n    classes.push({\n      name: currentClass,\n      columns: currentColumns,\n      column_count: currentColumns.length,\n    });\n  }\n\n  const totalColumns = classes.reduce((sum, c) => sum + c.column_count, 0);\n\n  return {\n    source_file: \"Picasso-EHI-Export-Documentation-V1_0-1-1.pdf\",\n    title: \"Amazing Charts EHI Export: Folder Organization and Data Format Specification\",\n    export_format: \"CSV/JSON/XML\",\n    data_classes: classes,\n    total_data_classes: classes.length,\n    total_columns: totalColumns,\n  };\n}\n\nasync function main() {\n  const picassoPdf = join(DOWNLOADS_DIR, [picassoText, acText] = await Promise.all([\n    extractText(picassoPdf),\n    extractText(acPdf),\n  ]);\n\n  console.log(\"Parsing Picasso-specific document...\");\n  const picassoResult = parsePicassoDoc(picassoText);\n\n  console.log(\"Parsing Amazing Charts document...\");\n  const acResult = parseAmazingChartsDoc(acText);\n\n  // Write outputs\n  writeFileSync(\n    join(ENRICHMENT_DIR, \"picasso-data-classes.json\"),\n    JSON.stringify(picassoResult, null, 2)\n  );\n  console.log(\n    `Picasso: ${picassoResult.total_data_classes} data classes, ${picassoResult.total_columns} total columns`\n  );\n\n  writeFileSync(\n    join(ENRICHMENT_DIR, \"amazing-charts-data-classes.json\"),\n    JSON.stringify(acResult, null, 2)\n  );\n  console.log(\n    `Amazing Charts: ${acResult.total_data_classes} data classes, ${acResult.total_columns} total columns`\n  );\n\n  // Summary\n  const summary = {\n    extraction_date: new Date().toISOString(),\n    files_discovered: 2,\n    files_parsed: 2,\n    parse_failures: [] as { file: string; error: string }[],\n    results: [\n      {\n        file: picassoResult.source_file,\n        data_classes: picassoResult.total_data_classes,\n        total_columns: picassoResult.total_columns,\n        export_format: picassoResult.export_format,\n      },\n      {\n        file: acResult.source_file,\n        data_classes: acResult.total_data_classes,\n        total_columns: acResult.total_columns,\n        export_format: acResult.export_format,\n      },\n    ],\n  };\n\n  writeFileSync(\n    join(ENRICHMENT_DIR, \"extraction-summary.json\"),\n    JSON.stringify(summary, null, 2)\n  );\n\n  console.log(\"\\nDone. Output files:\");\n  console.log(\"  picasso-data-classes.json\");\n  console.log(\"  amazing-charts-data-classes.json\");\n  console.log(\"  extraction-summary.json\");\n}\n\nmain().catch(console.error);\n"}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01N4Xz3nbMvgmXAqE53B8v1D","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01UbD2hFW48bzLi625w3wjjw","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/doc-tor-com--picasso/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# Doc-tor.com — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-15\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://doc-tor.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/Picasso-EHI-Export-Documentation-V1_0-1-1.pdf\n- CHPL IDs: 11652\n- Product: Picasso v8.2\n- Developer: Doc-tor.com (now owned by Harris Healthcare / Constellation Software)\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n### Step 1: Probe the registered URL\n```bash\ncurl -sI -L \"https://doc-tor.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/Picasso-EHI-Export-Documentation-V1_0-1-1.pdf\" \\\n  -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n```\nResult: HTTP 200, Content-Type: application/pdf, 195,305 bytes. Direct download, no redirects.\n\n### Step 2: Download the registered PDF\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://doc-tor.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/Picasso-EHI-Export-Documentation-V1_0-1-1.pdf\" \\\n  -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o Picasso-EHI-Export-Documentation-V1_0-1-1.pdf\n```\nConfirmed: PDF document, 8 pages, created 2023-10-16 by Kathiresan Palanisamy via Microsoft Word.\n\n**Critical finding**: Despite the filename containing \"Picasso,\" the document title is **\"Amazing Charts EHI Export: Folder Organization and Data Format Specification – v1.0\"**. This is the Amazing Charts sister product's data dictionary, not Picasso's own.\n\n### Step 3: Check the mandatory disclosures page for additional documentation\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://doc-tor.com/certified-healthcare-technology-cehrt-price-transparency/\" \\\n  -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o /tmp/doc-tor-disclosures.html\ngrep -oiE 'href=\"[^\"]*\\.(pdf|zip|xlsx|xls|csv|json|doc|docx|yaml|yml)[^\"]*\"' /tmp/doc-tor-disclosures.html\n```\nFound two additional PDFs:\n1. `http://doc-tor.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Picasso-EHI-Export-Documentation-V1_0-1.pdf` — a **Picasso-specific** EHI export document (different from the registered URL)\n2. `http://live.picassoemr.com/_PicassoAPI/PAA_API_documentation.pdf` — Picasso Application Access API documentation\n\n### Step 4: Download the Picasso-specific EHI export document\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://doc-tor.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Picasso-EHI-Export-Documentation-V1_0-1.pdf\" \\\n  -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o Picasso-EHI-Export-Documentation-V1_0-1.pdf\n```\nConfirmed: PDF document, 3 pages, created 2024-01-04 by Kathiresan Palanisamy. Title: **\"Picasso EHI Export: Folder Organization and Data Format Specification – v1.0\"**. This is the actual Picasso data dictionary with Picasso-specific column names and CSV-only format.\n\n### Step 5: Download the API documentation\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"http://live.picassoemr.com/_PicassoAPI/PAA_API_documentation.pdf\" \\\n  -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o PAA_API_documentation.pdf\n```\nConfirmed: PDF document, 4 pages, created 2023-01-10. Documents a SOAP/REST API (`ApplicationAccess.asmx`) that returns USCDI-compliant CCDs in XML format. This is a (g)(10)-style API, not the (b)(10) export mechanism.\n\n### Step 6: Verify no embedded URLs or attachments in PDFs\n```bash\npdftotext Picasso-EHI-Export-Documentation-V1_0-1-1.pdf - | grep -oiE 'https?://[^[:space:]>)\"]+' | sort -u\npdfdetach -list Picasso-EHI-Export-Documentation-V1_0-1-1.pdf\n```\nNo embedded URLs or file attachments found in any of the three PDFs.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThree PDF documents were collected, two of which are EHI export data dictionaries and one is a clinical API specification.\n\n### Document 1: Amazing Charts EHI Export (Registered URL — V1_0-1-1)\n- **8 pages**, 195 KB\n- Titled \"Amazing Charts EHI Export\" despite being hosted under a Picasso filename\n- Describes an export that creates per-patient folders with timestamped names\n- Supports three export formats: CSV, JSON, and XML\n- Contains a \"Documents\" subfolder for imported items, images, and related documents in original format\n- **44 data classes** with column-level detail (column names only, no data types or descriptions)\n- Supports single-patient and population-based export (by Provider, All Active, All Patients, or Encounter Range)\n- Data classes include: Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\n**Comparing the Picasso-specific document (21 data classes) against product research:**\n\n| Data Domain | Picasso Export | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Demographics | Yes | 51 columns including race, ethnicity, language, sex orientation, gender identity |\n| Allergies | Yes | 19 columns with RxNorm codes and severity |\n| Problems/Diagnoses | Yes | |\n| Clinical Notes | Yes | 15 columns — but notably simpler than Amazing Charts (just NOTETEXT + metadata vs. full SOAP structure) |\n| Encounters | Yes | 28 columns with facility info, E/M codes, diagnoses |\n| Care Team | Yes | 12 columns |\n| Family History | Yes | 7 columns with SNOMED codes |\n| Social History | Yes | 4 columns (sparse — just category/value pairs) |\n| Health Concerns | |\n| Tobacco/Smoking | Yes | 4 columns |\n| **Billing History** | **NO** | **Absent from Picasso-specific doc — present in Amazing Charts doc with 74 columns** |\n| **Patient Portal Messages** | **NO** | Not in either document |\n| **Documents/Attachments** | Partial | Referenced as \"Attachments\" subfolder preserving original format, but no data dictionary for metadata |\n| **E-Prescribing Details** | **NO** | No Rx transaction data (SureScripts status, pharmacy transmit, etc.) — present in Amazing Charts doc |\n| **Referrals** | **NO** | Present in Amazing Charts doc but absent from Picasso-specific doc |\n| **Scheduling/Appointments** | **NO** | Present in Amazing Charts doc but absent from Picasso-specific doc |\n| **Patient Generated Data** | **NO** | Present in Amazing Charts doc but absent from Picasso-specific doc |\n\n**The most significant gap is billing data.** Picasso is an integrated EHR + Practice Management + RCM suite that processes claims, payments, charges, and denial management. The product research highlights billing as a core capability. Yet the Picasso-specific EHI export document contains no billing data class at all. The Amazing Charts document (incorrectly linked as the registered URL) does include a comprehensive \"Billing History\" class with 74 columns covering CPT codes, ICD codes, fees, charges, NDC codes, modifiers, facility info, and referring provider info. It's unclear whether Picasso's actual export includes billing data using the Amazing Charts schema, or whether billing data is truly absent.\n\n### The Two-Document Problem\n\nThis vendor has a confusing documentation situation:\n\n1. The **registered URL** points to an **Amazing Charts** data dictionary (44 data classes, ~1,094 columns, CSV/JSON/XML). This is a different product — Amazing Charts is a sister product under the Harris Healthcare umbrella. The data class names, column names, and column counts are all different from Picasso.\n\n2. A **Picasso-specific** data dictionary exists (21 data classes, ~441 columns, CSV only) but was found only on the mandatory disclosures page, not at the registered URL. It has different column naming conventions (ALL_CAPS vs PascalCase) and a significantly narrower scope.\n\nThe relationship between these two documents is unclear. It could be:\n- Picasso's export was built from Amazing Charts' codebase and the Amazing Charts document is the more complete/accurate one\n- They are genuinely different exports for different products and the registered URL is simply wrong\n- The Picasso-specific document is a newer, reduced version that replaced the broader Amazing Charts export\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n- The Picasso export uses **CSV files** — one per data class per patient, organized in a folder structure\n- The Amazing Charts export additionally supports JSON and XML\n- No FHIR, C-CDA, or other healthcare standard is used for the bulk export (the separate API returns CCDs, but that's a different mechanism)\n- CSV is an appropriate format for a database-level export. Relationships between entities are implicit via shared IDs (PatientID, VisitID, ProviderID)\n- No formal schema definition (no JSON Schema, XSD, or DDL) — just column names in a PDF\n\n### Documentation Quality\n- **Readability**: The documents are clear but minimal — a simple two-column table mapping data class names to column names\n- **No field descriptions**: Only column names are provided. No data types, constraints, value sets, or cardinality information\n- **No examples**: No sample export files, sample records, or worked examples\n- **No export instructions**: Neither document explains how to trigger the export (which menu, which role has access, what parameters to set)\n- **No relationship documentation**: No explanation of how entities relate (e.g., how VISITID in Clinical Notes links to VISITID in Encounters)\n- **No value set documentation**: Coded fields like CODINGLANGUAGE, SEVERITYCODE, TYPE are listed but their allowed values are not defined\n- **Developer implementability**: A developer receiving this export would have column names but would need to reverse-engineer data types, relationships, and coded values from the actual exported data. Import implementation would be possible but require significant trial and error.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n- **Granularity**: Field-level (column names), but no data types or descriptions\n- **Coded fields**: Not documented with value sets\n- **Relationships**: Not documented — must be inferred from shared column names (PatientID, VisitID, etc.)\n- **Versioning**: Both documents are v1.0 with no change history\n- **The fundamental ambiguity**: The vendor has registered one product's data dictionary (Amazing Charts) as the documentation for a different product (Picasso), while also maintaining a separate Picasso-specific document that is narrower in scope. This makes it impossible to know with certainty what the actual Picasso EHI export contains.\n\n### Assessment Summary\n\nDoc-tor.com/Picasso has made a genuine attempt at (b)(10) compliance — the export is a database-level CSV dump organized by data class, not a FHIR/USCDI-only clinical summary. The Picasso-specific document covers 21 clinical and administrative data classes with field-level column listings. However, there are real concerns:\n\n1. **Billing data is the biggest gap.** For an integrated EHR/PM/RCM suite, the absence of billing, claims, and payment data from the Picasso-specific export is a significant omission.
